extracted.intended_audience: consultants, contractors, suppliers, governments, executing and implementing agencies, development institutions, private sector partners, and civil society/NGOs interested in doing business with ADB
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for vendors, consultants, contractors, and agencies on how ADB procures goods, works, non-consulting and consulting services, and how to register or find opportunities. Covers procurement categories, key governing documents, supplier registration instructions, and where to find tenders and notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register as a Supplier
rubrics_metrics.description: Interested vendors may email [email protected] with a message of intent to become an institutional (corporate) supplier of ADB with the (a) contact email address; and (b) registered business name for firms or complete name for individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear message of intent and the required identifying information; ADB lists Latest Institutional Procurement Notices and Major Contracts Awarded for reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational Procurement — Goods, Works, and Non-Consulting Services
rubrics_metrics.description: ADB extends loans and provides technical assistance to its developing member countries for a broad range of development projects and programs involving the procurement of goods, works, and services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational procurement is delivered through public and private sector operations, advisory services, and knowledge support; see Projects & Tenders for ongoing and future procurements and refer to ADB procurement policies and regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consulting Services — engagement types and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: ADB engages individual consultants and consulting entities to provide expert advice such as in contract preparation and project supervision, and to help ADB to prepare studies, appraisals, and reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consulting engagements may be administered by ADB or by ADB borrowers (see 'Consulting Services Administered by ADB Borrowers'); consult the Consultant Management System (CMS) and related guidance when pursuing consulting opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key Governing Documents and Policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance Notes on Procurement; Consulting Services Administered by ADB Borrowers; ADB Procurement Policy: Goods, Works, Nonconsulting and Consulting Services; Procurement Regulations for ADB Borrowers: Goods, Works, Nonconsulting and Consulting Services; Consultant Management System (CMS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These named policies, regulations and guidance notes are the primary references and rules that govern how procurements are run and how firms/individuals must comply when bidding or engaging with ADB-funded activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional/Corporate Procurement — purpose and sourcing
rubrics_metrics.description: ADB procures goods, works, and services necessary for institutional use in its headquarters and field offices to support its operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional procurement is separate from project procurement; those interested in institutional supplier opportunities should follow the 'Register as a Supplier' instruction and monitor institutional procurement notices and awarded contracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projects & Tenders — where to find notices
rubrics_metrics.description: See the list of ongoing and future procurement of goods, works, non-consulting, and consulting services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Projects & Tenders page to find specific procurement opportunities; more information pages exist tailored for consultants, contractors and suppliers, governments, executing and implementing agencies, development institutions, private sector partners, and civil society/NGOs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement Categories (what is procured)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procurement covers goods, works, non-consulting services, and consulting services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opportunities and rules differ by category; consult the Procurement Policy and Procurement Regulations to understand category-specific procedures and eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact and Outreach Channels
rubrics_metrics.description: ADB provides contact points and outreach: email for supplier registration, Subscriber Services, social media (X, YouTube, Facebook, Flickr, Instagram, LinkedIn), and links to Business Center, Projects & Tenders, Investor Relations, Data & Research, and other ADB sites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subscribe to newsletters, follow social channels, and use the provided email/contact pages to receive updates and alerts about procurement and business opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible Participant Types / Roles
rubrics_metrics.description: ADB identifies groups that can work with it: Consultants; Contractors and Suppliers; Governments; Executing and Implementing Agencies; Development Institutions; Private Sector Partners; Civil Society/Non-government Organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each participant type has dedicated guidance and pages explaining how to engage; check the relevant section for role-specific procedures, eligibility, and documentation requirements.
